paper_summary: Pure Mg reinforced with 5, 15 and 25 wt.% hollow glass microballoons (mean dia 11 um, density ~1.05 g/cc) was synthesized by disintegrated melt deposition (DMD) and characterized for density, CTE, elastic modulus and damping (impulse excitation, ASTM E1876-09). GMB addition reduced density by 13.4% (Mg-25: 1.47 g/cc), lowered modulus, and raised damping loss rate 12.5x (to ~108.2) and damping capacity ~370% (to 0.00256) versus pure Mg; Mg2Si secondary phase and matrix porosity were noted.

extraction_notes: Tables 1 (density, CTE) and 2 (elastic modulus, damping loss rate, damping capacity) were embedded as images and are NOT present in the text, so per-sample density, modulus and damping values for Mg-0/5/15 are left null; only values stated in text (Mg-25 density 1.47 g/cc, damping capacity 0.00256, loss rate ~108.2, attenuation coefficients for all four samples, pure Mg CTE 27.1 u/C) are recorded. Damping capacity Q^-1 was mapped to loss_tangent. Pure Mg CTE 27.1 u/C converted to 2.71e-5 1/K. Test type 'other' = impulse-excitation resonant damping (ASTM E1876), not DMA. Process route 'stir_casting' used for disintegrated melt deposition (stirred melt at 750 C, bottom poured with argon disintegration). Fractions are weight fractions; volume fractions not given. Linear fits L = 9.6373 + 3.9278*wt% and Q^-1 = 0.0006 + 8e-5*wt% are fits, not recorded as data.
